title: Basic Finance for Entrepreneurs
excerpt: Manage your business finances like a professional. Account separation, pricing and basic control.
author: Tu Emprendimiento
content:
Most entrepreneurs fail not for lack of talent but for lack of financial control. You don't need to be an accountant to manage your business money well. Here are the basics.

**Account separation is sacred**
Open a bank account exclusively for your business. Don't mix personal expenses with business expenses. This isn't just good practice — at some point you'll need to prove what is what (for taxes, for a loan, for a partner).

**Write everything down**
You don't need complex software. A spreadsheet or even a notebook can work. The important thing is to record: how much you sell, how much you spend, on what you spend. Without data you can't make decisions.

**Set prices with margin**
Most people set prices looking at what the competition does without calculating their own costs. Your price must cover: direct costs + operating expenses + your salary + profit margin. If you can't cover that, either raise the price or reduce costs.

**Always provision for taxes**
In Paraguay, taxes on personal income are progressive. A good practice is to set aside 15-20% of each income for taxes. If you don't do it, when SET comes you'll have a cash flow problem.
